hook_text: The towers lifted gold for a century. Here is what they left behind, what came before them, and who was not allowed in.
clip_script: Mining made South Africa's cities, and it left four stories your company must know. One: acid water. Flooded old mines plus pyrite make acid that carries iron and uranium into rivers, orange and dead, and the public pays billions to treat it. Two: dust. Bare dumps blow silica into Soweto and Riverlea every August. Three: before all of it, Iron Age smelters in Limpopo and KwaZulu-Natal ran clay furnaces with charcoal and skin bellows over a thousand years ago; that was technology, designed and refined by specialists. Four: women were banned underground by law until 1996 and are still a minority, with kit and facilities built for men. Pick one. Report it with three cited sources, more than one point of view, a conclusion the evidence holds, and what your design will do about it. A tender board expects a company that knows the ground it builds on.
visual_style: Four photographs on a whiteboard: orange stream, dust cloud, clay furnace, woman with cap lamp; a pyrite-to-acid reaction arrow; a furnace cross-section with bellows; a timeline 1911 to 1996 to 2004; a one-page report outline.
pacing: Acid, dust, iron, women, the report shape.
